sessions.title: FOMC Day Market Analysis (Wispr Flow recording)
sessions.summary: New York session on the FOMC-minutes day (release 14:00 ET; he says '11:00' on his Pacific clock). Choppy pre-news action, reduced lot size announced up front. US30 printed the only 5m double break down early; he waited for a Spotlight bearish confirmation or a proper retracement. US500 (weaker pair) then printed a 5m DB; he took a NAS sell anyway at reduced size, rolled on the first closure, and was wicked out at break-even. Later a US30 short off a 30s FVG and closure: rolled at the red dotted line (past the implied dealing range), told the room to take 50% and reduce to a 10% flyer before the Spotlight bearish confirmation printed; the confirmation printed and a retracement followed. His own broker was frozen so he could not take profit himself. Post-mortem: the NAS sell should not have been taken because a fresh DB means a 70-80% retracement into the range and the stronger pair retraces deeper. He also reviewed the prior day's Asia US30 trade (stop hunts on the 30s): an immediate rebalance is the entry and its line can never be moved; either demand a closure over the same old 30s line or take a new 30s FVG off the new leg (tap + close); his error was using the rebalance's entry without its FVG. Order block rule: when the DB leg is a single candle with no FVG, the candle's midpoint stands in for the 5m FVG step. Advised staying out of the PM session.

US500 printed a 5m DB; the tap back counted as the retracement. He demanded a candle body close plus an immediate rebalance at the zone, because wick-only touches become stop hunts. He flagged the 21:00 ET candle (his '6 o'clock' Pacific) as usually a displacement candle. NAS was preferred as the most consistent story (US30 had an untouched zone above; US500, the stronger pair, had no 5m bearish FVG), but NAS kept closing its 1m FVGs and gave no entry. NAS chopped at the blue zone, so he moved up to the 5m needing either a 5m bearish FVG or a cross plus reversal zone up; neither printed before the session ended. sessions.file: Live Session 2026-10-15 Purple and blue zone signals.txt
sessions.title: Purple and Blue Zone Signals (Wispr Flow recording)
sessions.summary: New York session on PPI day; no trades taken, mostly teaching. Purple zones are primarily Asia/London magnets, blue zones primarily NY; a zone layered with the NDOG is a highly magnetic target but still needs a signal setup (not 100% with high-impact news). Reversal areas: crossing one without a reversal zone painting is like a false M (original signal can still complete); after an M a cross is wanted, after a DB the retracement must stay between the DB line and the reversal area, a close past it means flip. Reversal zone invalidation: an opposite FVG on the zone's timeframe printing through it; FVGs both ways = void; with two zones start with the closest (prefer one with a blue zone). Fractal conflict play: a 1m DB crossing its line with a reversal zone can create the missing 5m FVG after a 5m M. Defer to the higher timeframe when 30s and 1m signal together. Consolidation = 5+ deadlocked candles; over 10 minutes means look at another asset. Max 1 hour per session, mark-up under 15 minutes, then a TradingView alert at the zone/FVG midpoint. Roll the stop the second a DB hits. No countertrend scalps of the post-DB retracement. Skipped a prior-session oil play (CPI day; would have won) and a late US index setup (PPI day): 'Do not be trading any US-related assets on PPI day, CPI day.' Zeus: same models on D/4H/15m, monthly FVG target, max 10% per stock / 20% per sector. Schedule: newbie session moves to Saturday 12:00 ET this week; today's Asia session is a Q&A at 8 PM ET.
